answers.answer:
1. I can't tell what this is from here, and I won't name a cause. A physio or sports doctor can examine the knee and tell you. Until they have, please don't run on it.

new.analysis:
## What the week showed

Most of the week went to plan, and the long run was the one real shortfall. The Wednesday tempo was done as written, with the four middle miles near 8:00 per mile, and the easy days stayed steady. Planned volume was 36 miles and you ran 32, and the whole gap sits on Sunday.

| Day | Planned | Ran | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tue Aug 11 | 6 mi easy | 6 mi | As planned |
| Wed Aug 12 | 8 mi with 4 mi at tempo | 8 mi | As planned |
| Thu Aug 13 | 5 mi easy | 5 mi | Right knee tight on the last hill |
| Sat Aug 15 | 4 mi easy | 4 mi | Knee a little tight before the run |
| Sun Aug 16 | 13 mi easy | 9 mi | Stopped and walked home |

Easy running was 76 percent of time in zones 1 and 2, under the 80 percent target. That is a minor point beside the knee.

## The knee

The pain rose through the week rather than settling, and that is why I am stopping running instead of adjusting it. It was tight on Thursday's last hill, a little tight before Saturday, then sharp on downhill sections from mile 7 on Sunday. You also said it now aches on stairs, and you have never had this before. I can't tell from here what is causing it, and I won't guess at a name; a physio or sports doctor can examine the knee and tell you.

## Why cross-training this week

Cross-training keeps your heart and legs working without the impact that loads the knee. Easy running at your usual volume would add the same stress you are trying to clear. Your base was in good shape before this, with about 32 to 35 miles a week and a 12 mile long run the week before.

## The way back

Once a professional clears you, I will restart with short, flat, easy runs at heart rate under 140, not with the 13 mile long run. Quality sessions and the long run come back last, once several easy runs feel normal. Ten weeks is enough to rebuild if the knee settles within about two weeks. A longer gap would put the under 3:45 goal at risk, and we would need to revisit the target then.
